verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents a first-party Scheduled flag changes feature that lets users define and schedule changes to a flag's targeting rules for future points in time. It also supports expiration dates for flag targeting, which covers time-bound changes. missing for 10: evidence that releases such as progressive or guarded rollouts can be scheduled to start at a future time, detail on scheduling via API/CLI, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can schedule flag changes and releases to happen at a specific future time

citations.quote: Scheduling flag changes lets you define and schedule changes to your flag's targeting rules for future points in time.
You can even set expiration dates for flag targeting if you know you only want customers to receive a flag for a specific period of time.
